tagline: Jinx's hexplosive debut video, and the first step toward Arcane.
headline: A Norwegian rock singer and a small Paris studio turned Jinx's launch into the music video that led to Arcane.
summary: Riot uploaded "Get Jinxed" on October 8, 2013, two days before Jinx went live, at a time when a champion getting a song with its own animated music video was something new. Sung by Djerv's Agnete Kjølsrud over music by Riot's Christian Linke and animated by the small Paris studio Fortiche, the video helped make Jinx one of League's best-loved champions and has now passed 150 million views. It was also Riot's first project with Fortiche, the partnership that went on to make Arcane, where Jinx sings part of the song herself.

story.heading: Two days before Jinx
story.body:
At the end of September 2013, Riot announced Jinx as League's next champion: a manic gunslinger who swaps between a minigun called Pow-Pow and a rocket launcher called Fishbones. On October 8, two days before she went live with patch 3.12, Riot uploaded *Get Jinxed* to the League of Legends YouTube channel. Riot had made cinematic trailers before, and Vi had arrived in December 2012 as the first champion with a login screen built around an original song with lyrics. A full song with its own animated music video was new, though. Looking back in 2023, Millenium wrote that nobody saw it coming, and Engadget has called it League's first character-driven cinematic.

The press picked it up the next day. CG Channel featured it in its "Eye candy" column, pointing out that Riot had made not just a login screen or a cinematic but a complete 3D animated music video, and it compared the look to the work of Jamie Hewlett.

story.heading: A rock voice from Norway
story.body:
The voice belongs to Agnete Kjølsrud, a Norwegian singer who fronted the alternative metal band Animal Alpha until 2009 and has led the hard rock band Djerv since it formed that year. Riot's Christian "Praeco" Linke wrote the music, and the official release credits him as composer and lyricist. The song is sung from Jinx's point of view. She feels ignored and bored, she wants a little anarchy, and she dares the listener to come play and try a little harder to catch her. Kjølsrud's snarling, playful delivery gave Jinx a personality before most players had even picked her.

Riot treated the track as a real release. The video description linked to the song on SoundCloud, the track became the theme of Jinx's login screen, and on January 28, 2015 it appeared as track 13 of *The Music of League of Legends Vol. 1*.

story.heading: Fortiche's first job for Riot
story.body:
Pascal Charrue, Jérôme Combe and Arnaud Delord founded Fortiche Production in Paris in 2009, and in 2013 it was still a small studio that mostly made music videos and commercials. In Riot's tenth-anniversary making-of, the team explains that they had made a short clip for friends, partly to test camera mapping. Christian Linke found it somehow and tried to contact them, but they admit they never answered the phone back then. *Get Jinxed* was the first time they put together a real team to work in their own style, mixing 2D and 3D.

They had little time for tests, so they focused on a few iconic shots and built the video as a series of "stage tableaux", each showing a different facet of Jinx. They had her ride a rocket like a surfboard because she is punk. They gave her a lip-biting habit that, they joke, every Jinx cosplayer now copies. And they added a cymbal-banging toy monkey as a small animal that expresses her madness. The 2D artists they hired for the explosions were, they say, the team that now leads 2D effects on *Arcane*.

story.heading: Love at first explosion
story.body:
Jinx became a fan favourite almost immediately. On the video's fifth anniversary in 2018, Dot Esports called her launch one of the most hyped champion releases in the game's history. It argued that her gleeful, slightly psychotic energy stood out among champions built on battle, shadows and raw power, and it credited the music video with showing her personality in a way the game alone could not. Fan art, cosplay and fan fiction poured out. Know Your Meme notes that the video also inspired fan-made remakes, from a *Danganronpa* AMV uploaded about a month later to a Source Filmmaker remake in December 2014. The League wiki, meanwhile, catalogues the in-jokes hidden in the video, from "Nerf Heimerdinger" graffiti to Tibbers lying on a pile of wrecked robots.

The views kept climbing. Know Your Meme counted more than 110 million within eight years, and as of October 2026 the official video stands at about 152.8 million, the 14th most-viewed upload on League's YouTube channel. Every video ranked above it was released in 2014 or later. On Spotify the track has passed 158 million streams, and Djerv's label says it had passed 250 million streams across platforms by 2025.

story.heading: Still on stage
story.body:
*Get Jinxed* has also lived on away from the screen. Riot held League of Legends Live, a concert at the Beijing National Aquatics Center, on the eve of the 2017 World Championship final, and *Get Jinxed* was billed among the League hits on the programme alongside Star Guardian and *The Curse of the Sad Mummy*. Djerv now play it at rock festivals. Setlist.fm lists it in their Tons of Rock set in Oslo in June 2025, right before *Rebel Heart*, and in their Copenhell set in Copenhagen in June 2026.

Other bands have taken it up as well. On November 23, 2024, the Korean band QWER played a free show at Riot's *Arcane* Season 2 Fan Fest in Seoul's Seongsu district, and a fan recording from the day shows *Get Jinxed* in their set.

story.heading: The road to Arcane
story.body:
The biggest legacy of *Get Jinxed* is the partnership behind it. When Riot announced an equity investment in Fortiche in March 2022, it named *Get Jinxed* as the two companies' first collaboration and listed what followed: *Warriors* and *Enemy* with Imagine Dragons, the Ekko cinematic *Seconds*, K/DA's *POP/STARS* and the Worlds 2018 anthem *RISE*. Christian Linke and Alex Yee both worked on the video. They went on to create *Arcane*, Riot's animated series made with Fortiche, and chose Jinx and her sister Vi as its leads. Linke told Engadget that the two characters already got "special treatment" because the team simply liked them.

*Arcane* returns the favour with nods to the video. Netflix's own guide to the show's League easter eggs points out that Jinx turns one of her cymbal monkeys into a Hextech crystal bomb. It also notes that in episode 4 she sings part of *Get Jinxed* while examining blueprints for the hex crystal stabilizer. In the 2023 making-of, Fortiche's artists say the freedom they had and the meeting with Riot are what brought them all to *Arcane*.

story.heading: Ten years on, a rebel heart
story.body:
For the video's tenth anniversary in September 2023, Riot Games Music released *10 Years of "Get Jinxed"*, in which Fortiche's artists look back at their first Riot project. They admit it has aged a bit and call it a do-it-yourself production, but they say the studio's style was already there. Some shots still hold up for them, like the one of Jinx surrounded by explosions.

A year later the voice came back too. Djerv recorded *Rebel Heart* for the *Arcane* Season 2 soundtrack, their second collaboration with League, and Riot Games Music released its visualizer in November 2024. Kjølsrud said it was "wonderful to feel the presence of Jinx again".

whyItMatters: It was one of the first times Riot introduced a champion with an original song and a full animated music video, released two days before Jinx went live.
It was Riot's first project with Fortiche, the partnership that later produced POP/STARS, RISE and the Netflix series Arcane, created by two of the video's makers, Christian Linke and Alex Yee.
It gave Jinx a voice and a personality before anyone had played her, helping build one of League's biggest fandoms.
About 152.8M views make it the 14th most-viewed upload on League's YouTube channel and the oldest video in that top 14. Djerv's label says it has passed 250M streams across platforms.
Arcane pays it back directly: Jinx sings part of the song in episode 4, a cymbal monkey becomes one of her bombs, and Djerv returned for Season 2 with Rebel Heart.
More than a decade later it is still performed live, by Djerv at European rock festivals and by QWER at the Arcane Season 2 Fan Fest in Seoul.

communityMoments.title: The video drops
communityMoments.description: Riot uploaded Get Jinxed (ft. Djerv) to the League of Legends channel, describing it as Jinx's dreams coming alive in a sequence packed with bombs and bullets.

communityMoments.title: Jinx goes live
communityMoments.description: Two days after the video, Jinx became playable during patch 3.12. Millenium later wrote that she probably had the best debut of any new champion.

communityMoments.title: Fans start remaking it
communityMoments.description: About a month after release, a fan-made Danganronpa AMV set to Get Jinxed went up on YouTube, one of the first of many fan videos and remakes the song inspired.

communityMoments.title: On The Music of League of Legends Vol. 1
communityMoments.description: Get Jinxed was track 13 of The Music of League of Legends Vol. 1, alongside themes like Demacia Rising and The Curse of the Sad Mummy.

communityMoments.title: Billed for League of Legends Live in Beijing
communityMoments.description: Riot's concert at the Beijing National Aquatics Center on the eve of the Worlds 2017 final listed Get Jinxed among the League hits to be performed.

communityMoments.title: Happy fifth birthday
communityMoments.description: Dot Esports marked the video's fifth anniversary with a tribute to Jinx's fandom, calling Get Jinxed the music video that started it all.

communityMoments.title: Jinx sings it in Arcane
communityMoments.description: In Arcane episode 4, Jinx sings part of Get Jinxed while examining blueprints for the hex crystal stabilizer. Netflix also pointed out a cymbal monkey turned into a bomb.

communityMoments.title: Riot invests in Fortiche
communityMoments.description: Announcing an equity investment in Arcane's studio, Riot named the Get Jinxed music video as the start of the partnership.

communityMoments.title: 10 Years of Get Jinxed
communityMoments.description: For the video's tenth anniversary, Riot Games Music released a making-of in which Fortiche's artists look back at their first Riot project.

communityMoments.title: Djerv return with Rebel Heart
communityMoments.description: Djerv came back to Jinx with Rebel Heart for the Arcane Season 2 soundtrack, and Riot Games Music released its official visualizer.

communityMoments.title: QWER play it at the Arcane Fan Fest
communityMoments.description: Korean band QWER performed Get Jinxed during their free show at the Arcane Season 2 Fan Fest in Seongsu, Seoul, and a fan recording of the performance went up the same day.

communityMoments.title: Live at Tons of Rock
communityMoments.description: Djerv played Get Jinxed, followed by Rebel Heart, at Tons of Rock in Oslo.

communityMoments.title: Live at Copenhell
communityMoments.description: Get Jinxed was again part of Djerv's festival set, this time at Copenhell in Copenhagen.

keyMoments.label: The wind-up monkey
keyMoments.description: A toy cymbal monkey sits in Jinx's room as the song gets going. Fortiche added it as a small animal that expresses her madness, and Arcane later brought it back.

keyMoments.label: Surfing a rocket
keyMoments.description: Jinx rides one of a swarm of graffiti-covered rockets like a surfboard across a sunset sky. Fortiche's team says they did it "because she's punk".

keyMoments.label: A look over the shoulder
keyMoments.description: Walking down a green-lit tunnel, Jinx turns and grins back at the camera.

keyMoments.label: First chorus
keyMoments.description: The band crashes in, robots light up in the dark, and Jinx opens fire with her minigun Pow-Pow.

keyMoments.label: A dance with a robot
keyMoments.description: On a spotlit stage, Jinx waltzes with one of her mechanical victims.

keyMoments.label: Jinx was here!
keyMoments.description: Jinx rides a rhino covered in her pink and blue graffiti, with "Jinx was here!" scrawled on its side, past a burning gate.

keyMoments.label: Balloon ride
keyMoments.description: Jinx swings from a bunch of balloons high above the land. The League wiki notes that they carry the skull insignia of Ziggs's bombs.

keyMoments.label: Explosions all around
keyMoments.description: Jinx stands beneath the city's towers as explosions burst all around her, a shot Fortiche's artists say still holds up.

keyMoments.label: A bath of bullets
keyMoments.description: During the quieter bridge, Jinx lounges in a bathtub filled with ammunition.

keyMoments.label: Final chorus: the robot hall
keyMoments.description: The last chorus kicks in as Jinx storms a glass-roofed hall full of robots with Pow-Pow and Fishbones.

keyMoments.label: Queen of the scrapheap
keyMoments.description: Tibbers lies among a pile of wrecked robots, and Jinx poses on top of it with a gun on her shoulder as lightning cracks behind her.

keyMoments.label: The giant monkey
keyMoments.description: A giant cymbal monkey looms behind her in a flash of pink, the shot Fortiche calls the hardest to make.

keyMoments.label: Only a dream
keyMoments.description: The music fades and Jinx is back at her table beside her toy monkey, as if waking from the dream the rampage came from.

keyMoments.label: Tagging the logo
keyMoments.description: Jinx's pink spray paint is slapped across the League of Legends logo.

keyMoments.label: How Riot found Fortiche
keyMoments.description: The team recalls a short clip made for friends that Christian Linke somehow found, and the calls they never answered.

keyMoments.label: The future Arcane VFX team
keyMoments.description: Fortiche explains that it hired 2D artists for the explosions, and that this is when it met the team that leads 2D effects on Arcane.

keyMoments.label: Why she surfs the bomb
keyMoments.description: The artists explain the rocket-surfing shot and the lip-biting habit that cosplayers picked up.

keyMoments.label: The monkey's legacy
keyMoments.description: The cymbal monkey, they say, was meant to express a bit of madness, stuck in players' minds and later turned up in Arcane.

keyMoments.label: The road to Arcane
keyMoments.description: The team calls it a do-it-yourself production where the style was already there, and credits the meeting with Riot for bringing them all to Arcane.

featuredClip.description: Jinx surfs a rocket scrawled with 'HA HA' through a sunset sky full of missiles, the signature image of the video.
